dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Lord Barbatos, please hear my wishes on the wind...

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: What's that pleasant aroma... Huh? It's perfume, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: I'm listening to the sound of wind... and the voices of the people.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: With so many merchants and sailors coming and going, it's natural for them to bring more than just goods, but also secrets and sins buried deep within their hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Lending an ear to their confessions and soothing their souls — that is the duty of the Church of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Goodbye. May the Anemo Archon protect you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't see a church around here...

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Of course. This is Dornman Port, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Long before the Anemo Archon toppled the rule of the tower's tyrant, this land was already a fief of the Gunnhildr Clan, and it was here that they established Mondstadt's very first sacred sanctuary.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: But during the dark age of the old aristocracy, the Church gradually devolved into a mere puppet of the aristocracy.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: To signal a total break from the increasingly tyrannical Imunlaukr Clan, the Gunnhildrs of the time seized the bishop sent from Mondstadt, hurled him from the window of the sanctuary's high tower, and subsequently tore it down.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: To the Church of Favonius, the Gunnhildr Clan's actions were the true act of piety — a refusal to coexist with those who commit evil in the name of faith.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: That's why the sanctuary was never rebuilt ever since... and why this place remains roofless to this very day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the Dornman Port belongs to the Gunnhildr Clan?

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: No. After Vennessa's uprising, the Gunnhildr Clan led a push to abolish all hereditary noble fiefdoms, returning both the land and their freedom to the people of Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Look at the present day. The once-mighty Imunlaukr Clan has seen its bloodline vanish, and their accomplices have long since lost their former prominence.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Time eventually erodes all mighty powers with no partiality, and only the wind continues to blow as it always has. This is also a blessing from Lord Barbatos.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About fragrances...

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Hmm... your fragrance is quite distinctive. Fresh, but not overly sweet. Like the breeze that drifts across Starsnatch Cliff in early spring.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Many people wear perfume before coming to confession. Much like prayer, confession is a solemn sacrament. And as Millhaven nearby happens to produce so many fragrances, it's only natural...

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: But yours feels gentler. There's something about it that settles the heart.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: If a fragrance like this lingered here while they listened to confessions... perhaps those who come weighed down with sorrow might find their spirits loosening, if only a little.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Mr. Lohen, I feel we must talk about the matter of confession...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh? Have I done something that requires confession? You'll have to forgive me, I can't seem to recall anything.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Do you remember... Struwell? And the others?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ah, the three noisy brats. I remember them.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: A few days ago, they came to me in floods of tears, practically begging to confess to some pranks.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh? Interesting. What did they do?

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: ...Sneak into Granny Marthe's house with the grand plan of smearing cream onto her face.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: But when Moricztill was keeping watch, a gust of wind rang the bell above his head, scaring him so much that he fled immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Then, just as Max was planning to sneak into the room, another gust of wind knocked over a honey jar by his feet. That woke Granny Marthe up immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: Finally, when Struwell was making his frantic escape, a sudden gust of wind brushed his back. Only when he reached his friends did he find a slip of paper clinging to him...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: —Let me guess... was it, "The Anemo Archon is always watching"?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Heh. Isn't it a wonderful trade? The world loses three little troublemakers and gains three devout believers in the Anemo Archon... though I'd give them two days, at most.

dialogues.speaker: Hannelore
dialogues.text: *spluttering* Mr. Lohen! Regardless of your motives, there's a limit to how much you should be terrorizing children. Dragging the Anemo Archon's name into it is equally uncalled for!
